svg.title: Copier refuses an answer the new project could not use: Copier refuses a malformed Docker answer, and the CI file stays valid YAML whatever the address holds
svg.text: Copier refuses an answer the new project could not use
Scenario: Copier refuses a malformed Docker answer, and the CI file stays valid YAML whatever the address holds

g.text: When a project on its own runners gets a Docker address without tcp://, a relative
certificate folder and an unknown storage driver, and Copier refuses each one
A project whose CI runs on its own GitLab runners answers three Docker questions. The loop gives each one a common
mistake: an address without tcp://, a certificate folder that is not a full path, and overlay, a storage driver Docker
Copier refuses all three, each on the line under its answer. The first two messages say what to type instead. The driver
gets "Invalid choice": it can only be one of five names. ls finds no runner folder, --overwrite or not.

text.tspan: for answer in gitlab_docker_host=docker:2376 gitlab_docker_tls_certdir=certs gitlab_docker_driver=overlay; do
--data ci_platform=gitlab_self_hosted --data "$answer" /workspace runner 2>&1 | tail -n 1; done; ls -d runner

g.text: Then an address with a space after its colon still gives a CI file that yamllint accepts
This address starts right, but a space slipped in after its colon: tcp://docker: 2376. Copier only checks how an address
The CI file holds the address in quotes, "tcp://docker: 2376". task yamllint, the project's own YAML check, ends on "All
files correctly linted with yamllint!": the CI file is valid YAML.
